claims.scope: Delta_B is the same all-point discrepancy as D_B in Section 30; primitive counts include both signs, with half-count only for symmetric bodies.
hypotheses: Fixed convex body containing zero; shortest nonzero lattice gauge one.

claims.scope: Reversing the finite large-divisor sum gives the lattice sum M(L/r(m))-M(D) over 0<r(m)<=L/D.
hypotheses: D is integer, 1<=D<=L; M is defined with floor cutoff.
claims.proof_notes: For each m, the permitted integers are D<d<=L/r(m). Boundary terms with floor(L/r)=D vanish; no upper cutoff is omitted because A_B(u)=0 below one.

finite_computation.limit: Exact finite rational examples only; no geometric modulus, infinite-range bound or arithmetic hypothesis is established.

claims.scope: A_B(U)<<_B U^2 and partial summation give sum(r(m)^-1,0<r<=U)<<_B U.
hypotheses: U>=1; lattice minimum one.
claims.proof_notes: The exact summation formula is A_B(U)/U+integral_1^U A_B(u)/u^2 du; the lower endpoint convention includes lattice points of gauge one.

claims.scope: Partial summation bounds abs(sum(mu(d)/d^2,d>D)) by O(C*eta(D)/D).
hypotheses: |M(x)|<=C*x*eta(x); eta>=0 and nonincreasing.
claims.proof_notes: The tail is -M(D)/D^2+2*integral_D^infinity M(t)/t^3 dt; bounded eta makes the endpoint at infinity vanish.

finite_computation.limit: Exact finite rational examples only; no geometric modulus, infinite-range bound or arithmetic hypothesis is established.

claims.scope: The small-divisor geometric discrepancy plus L^2*eta(D)/D bounds the primitive remainder; eta(x)=x^(theta-1) gives L^2 D^(theta-2).
hypotheses: Same Mertens/envelope hypothesis; 0<=theta<1 for the power form.
claims.proof_notes: Bound both M(L/r) and M(D) using eta(D). This explicitly pays for the geometric counting variation; pointwise discrepancy size alone cannot be multiplied by |M|.

claims.scope: The small-divisor sum is at most 2L times the logarithmic modulus integral from L/(D+1) to L.
hypotheses: L/(D+1)>=1; decreasing geometric envelope.

claims.scope: The geometric Dini condition implies E_B(L)=o_B(L), using only the unconditional PNT form M(x)=o(x).
hypotheses: Integral_1^infinity omega(u)/u du is finite.
claims.proof_notes: Use eta(x)=sup(y>=x)|M(y)|/y. Fix U>=2 and take D=floor(L/U); the normalized tail tends to zero at fixed U, then the small-divisor integral tends to zero as U grows. No RH input is used.

claims.scope: A fixed zeta-zero-free half-plane Re(s)>theta0 gives M(x)=O_epsilon(x^(theta0+epsilon)) for every epsilon>0.
hypotheses: 1/2<=theta0<1; the pole at one is excluded from the nonvanishing statement.
claims.proof_notes: The chapter now gives explicit zero-free disks, a log-zeta branch, polynomial strip growth, Borel-Caratheodory and three-circles exponent lambda<1. This bounds 1/zeta by every height power on smaller half-planes. Half-integer truncated Perron inversion with T=x^2 then yields the sharp cutoff bound. No claim about a general Dirichlet series is made.

claims.scope: The family of Mertens bounds gives a locally uniformly convergent Mellin representation for 1/zeta throughout Re(s)>theta0, hence excludes zeta zeros there.
hypotheses: For every epsilon>0, M(x)=O_epsilon(x^(theta0+epsilon)).
claims.proof_notes: On each compact choose epsilon below its distance from theta0, then use partial summation and analytic continuation.

claims.scope: The pinned September manuscript claims the 7/8 half-plane for finite-order Hecke characters over Q(sqrt(-3)) and Dirichlet L-functions, including zeta.
claims.coverage_gap: Neither full proof nor formalization/correspondence was independently verified; 7/8+epsilon Mertens input remains hypothetical in this chapter.

claims.scope: The pinned October manuscript claims the separate 11/12 result and calls it an intermediate step toward the September statement.
claims.coverage_gap: Neither full proof nor formalization/correspondence was independently verified; no later revision or publication status is inferred.

claims.scope: Any fixed Mertens power theta<1 and geometric u/(log u)^beta imply primitive L*(log L)^(1-beta); beta=1 gives O(L).
hypotheses: Geometric estimate for all u>=3; beta>0; M(x)<<x^theta, theta<1.
claims.proof_notes: Choose 1/(2-theta)<d<1 and D=floor(L^d). The tail is a smaller fixed power than L and the integral over log u in [(1-d)log L+O(1),log L] has order (log L)^(1-beta), including beta=1.

claims.scope: The unconditional Vinogradov-Korobov Mertens estimate is the one recorded in Zhai equation (1.5).
The three beta rows follow by integrating t^-beta from a*F(L)+O(1) to log L after an exponential cutoff.
hypotheses: Same geometric logarithmic bound; classical VK Mertens bound.
claims.proof_notes: D=floor(L exp(-aF(L))) with a small fixed positive a; F(D)/F(L)->1. Rates are L log(L)^(1-beta) for beta<1, L log log L for beta=1, and L F(L)^(1-beta) for beta>1. No optimality is asserted.

claims.scope: Balancing L^alpha D^(1-alpha) with L^2 D^(theta-2) gives d=(2-alpha)/(3-alpha-theta) and kappa=(2-alpha*theta)/(3-alpha-theta).
hypotheses: 0<=alpha<1; 0<=theta<1; both geometric and Mertens bounds hold.
claims.proof_notes: The cutoff exponent lies in (0,1). At alpha=2/3, theta=1/2,7/8,11/12 gives 10/11,34/35,50/51. Epsilon losses are renamed; none of these assigns alpha=2/3 to a torus norm ball.

finite_computation.limit: Exact finite rational examples only; no geometric modulus, infinite-range bound or arithmetic hypothesis is established.

claims.scope: A fixed geometric power saving plus VK yields L exp(-c_B F(L)) for some positive constant.
hypotheses: |Delta_B(u)|<<u^alpha, 0<=alpha<1; VK Mertens bound.
claims.proof_notes: Small divisor term is L exp(-a(1-alpha)F(L)), while the tail is L exp(-(c-a+o(1))F(L)); choose 0<a<c.

claims.scope: Zhai equation (1.4) is an unconditional sublinear primitive comparison for the stated smooth, positively curved convex class.
hypotheses: Finite nonzero curvature everywhere; one-to-one C4 Gauss map; zero is interior.
claims.proof_notes: Area parameter x=L^2 changes x^(1/2)exp(-cF(x)) into L exp(-c_new F(L)). These hypotheses are not imposed on the torus norm ball.

claims.scope: Baker Theorem 1 gives O_epsilon(L^(10/13+epsilon)) for its specified domain class under RH.
hypotheses: RH and all of (H1)-(H4): positive continuous radial graph, piecewise C4 nonzero-curvature arcs, no tangent through zero, no single arc containing both horizontal/vertical tangents, C4 reciprocal arcs, rational endpoint tangent slopes.
claims.proof_notes: Statement comparison only, no external proof audit or assertion of the best current exponent.

claims.scope: Strict convexity alone still gives only an unspecified o(L log L) rate in this transfer scheme even with a fixed Mertens power saving.
hypotheses: Same geometric envelope; choose the fixed cutoff exponent used above.
claims.proof_notes: Bound the modulus by its value at cL^(1-d); total variation of A_B(L/d) on a divisor dyadic block can be order (L/D)^2. This is an insufficiency of these inputs, not a general impossibility theorem.

claims.scope: Z_B^prim(s)=Z_B(s)/zeta(s) for Re(s)>2, and the discrepancy integral continues the numerator meromorphically to Re(s)>1 with the area pole at two.
hypotheses: Gauge minimum one; all-point discrepancy O(u), in particular o(u) under strict convexity.
claims.proof_notes: Positive multiples give the absolutely convergent product; Stieltjes summation gives a_B*s/(s-2)+s*integral_1^infinity Delta_B(u)u^(-s-1)du. A zero-free denominator does not provide continuation/growth of the numerator through Re(s)=1.

claims.scope: The explicit flat-point/rational-normal construction excludes every fixed primitive sublinear power bound for that body, without excluding O(L) or o(L).
hypotheses: All hypotheses of prop:normballflatrow and the local graph-flatness bounds.

claims.scope: For all lattice points the same empty contact row and microscopic increment imply max(|Delta(L)|,|Delta(L+1/L)|)>=L W(h/L^2)/2-O_B(1). Therefore O(L/log L) requires W(h/L^2)=O(1/log L) on contact scales.
hypotheses: Same rational supporting normal, two-sided upper graph, irrational alpha/h, and L=n/h; now every sufficiently large integer n is allowed.
claims.proof_notes: Count all row integers with w+O(1), without a phi(n)/n density factor. The area increment is a_B*(2+L^-2). The local double-exponential profile has W~(log log L)^(-1/beta), which violates the proposed necessary condition.

claims.scope: A quantitative all-point modulus compatible with a specified torus ball remains unproved here; O(L/log L) is only a candidate conditional target.
The all-point O(L/log L) remainder is equivalent to the same bound for A_B(2L)-4A_B(L), with the usual quadratic asymptotic.
hypotheses: Fixed body; large L>1; statement concerns a uniform infinite range.
claims.proof_notes: Forward implication uses log(2L)~log L. Reverse implication bounds each inverse term by 2^-j L/log L and sums the geometric series.
